section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The Running Cheetah
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of rate of change using a cheetah: Position (m), Velocity (m/s), and Acceleration (m/s²). Explain that just as velocity is the derivative of position, acceleration is the derivative of velocity—forming a 'chain of rates'.
section_1.example: Visualizing a cheetah accelerating: Plotting position vs. time (a curve), velocity vs. time (the slope of the curve), and acceleration (the slope of the velocity).

section_2.title: Defining Higher Order Derivatives
section_2.content: Formalize the notation: f'(x) is the 1st derivative, f''(x) is the 2nd derivative, and fⁿ⁾(x) represents the n-th derivative. Emphasize that each step measures the 'rate of change of the previous rate'.
section_2.example: Mathematical notation evolution: f(x) → f'(x) → f''(x) → f'''(x) → f⁽⁴⁾(x), showing how the power rule (d/dx xⁿ) cascades.

section_3.title: Geometric Interpretation: Concavity
section_3.content: Connect the 2nd derivative to the physical shape of the graph. f''(x) > 0 indicates 'Concave Up' (like a cup holding water), while f''(x) < 0 indicates 'Concave Down' (like an umbrella shedding rain).
section_3.example: An animated graph of f(x) = x³ transitioning from concave down to concave up at the inflection point x=0, with dynamic tangent lines demonstrating the change.

section_4.title: Step-by-Step Calculation Practice
section_4.content: Walk through a polynomial differentiation sequence. Use a simple cubic function to demonstrate that the higher the derivative, the simpler the function becomes until it reaches zero.

section_5.title: Summary & Real-World Application
section_5.content: Recap: 1st derivative = Velocity/Slope; 2nd derivative = Acceleration/Concavity. Briefly mention that higher order derivatives are essential in engineering for 'Jerk' (the 3rd derivative) in elevator design to ensure passenger comfort.
section_5.example: An animation of an elevator starting smoothly vs. abruptly, controlled by the 3rd derivative of position (Jerk).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
